    18	  `H:homog` and `α < 2`, and a continuous, nonnegative, nonzero, compactly

    21	\subsection{Global bounds and the unmasked spectral bottom}
    22	
    23	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian envelope for the original covariance]
    24	  \label{L:variational-heat-envelope}
    25	  For the normalized heat kernel $p_\epsilon(x) =
    26	  (2\pi\epsilon)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/(2\epsilon)}$,
    27	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-heat-envelope}
    28	    (\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    29	    =\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}\mu(\ud\xi),
    30	    \qquad
    31	    0\le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    32	    \le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(0)<\infty.
    33	  \end{equation}
    34	  The value at zero is strictly positive.
    35	\end{lemma}
    36	
    37	\begin{proof}
    38	  A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial ball growth. Indeed, evaluate
    39	  its tempered bound on a nonnegative smooth cutoff equal to one on $B_1$,
    40	  dilated by $R \ge 1$. Its finitely many Schwartz seminorms are bounded by
    41	  $CR^N$, so positivity gives a ball-mass bound $CR^N$. Summing dyadic annuli
    42	  shows that $(1+|x|)^{-L}$ is integrable for $L > N$. Apply this separately to
    43	  $\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Gaussian weights are therefore integrable against both
    44	  measures. The classical convolution on the left is finite and smooth locally
    45	  in $x$: on compact $x$ sets its translated Gaussian derivatives are bounded by
    46	  any fixed sufficiently fast polynomial weight in the integration variable.
    47	
    48	  Pair the convolution with a Schwartz test $\varphi$. Absolute Fubini is
    49	  justified by these weights. The resulting pairing is that of $\Gamma$ with
    50	  $p_\epsilon*\varphi$. Applying the spectral convention in
    51	  Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} and the identity $\int p_\epsilon(y)e^{-i\xi\cdot
    52	  y}\ud y = e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}$ gives exactly the right side
    53	  of~\eqref{E:variational-heat-envelope} as a distribution. The heat kernel is
    54	  even, so either Fourier sign gives that same Gaussian multiplier. Its spectral
    55	  integral is absolutely finite and continuous in $x$ by dominated convergence.
    56	  Thus, equality of the two continuous distributions gives equality at every
    57	  $x$, without an extra normalization factor. The physical convolution is
    58	  nonnegative. Evenness of $\mu$ makes the spectral integral real, and its
    59	  absolute value is bounded by its total Gaussian mass, the value at zero.
    60	  Finally, $\Gamma \ne 0$ and $p_\epsilon > 0$ give strict positivity there.
    61	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope}.
    62	\end{proof}

    64	\begin{lemma}[Global regularity of the original mean]
    65	  \label{L:variational-global-mean}
    66	  Every mixed time and space derivative of $h_s$ is globally bounded in space,
    67	  uniformly on compact time intervals. In particular, for $I = [0,1]$ there are
    68	  finite constants $M,C_\Psi$ such that
    69	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-global-mean}
    70	    0\le h_s(x)\le M,\qquad
    71	    \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty\le C_\Psi|s-t|,
    72	    \qquad s,t\in I.
    73	  \end{equation}
    74	\end{lemma}
    75	
    76	\begin{proof}
    77	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time; its compact support inside $(0,1)$ makes this a
    78	  smooth extension. For any mixed derivative $D\Psi$, a fixed $\epsilon > 0$ and
    79	  compactness of its common spatial support give $|D\Psi(t,x)| \le
    80	  C_Dp_\epsilon(x)$ for all $t,x$. Here the heat kernel has a positive minimum
    81	  on that support. Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope} consequently bounds
    82	  $\Gamma*|D\Psi(t,\cdot)|$ uniformly in $t,x$. Ordinary local differentiation
    83	  against the Radon measure gives the corresponding derivatives of the
    84	  convolution. After the change $r = s-t$,
    85	  \[
    86	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
    87	    (\Gamma*\Psi(s-r,\cdot))(x)\ud r.
    88	  \]
    89	  For $s$ in a compact interval the relevant $r$ lie in a fixed bounded
    90	  interval. The preceding global bound times $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable since $a <
    91	  1$. Every derivative thus falls on the smooth test and passes through the
    92	  integral by dominated convergence, with the claimed global spatial bounds.
    93	  Nonnegativity follows from positive kernels. The bounded time derivative
    94	  proves the Lipschitz estimate. No directional decay of the mean has been
    95	  inferred. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-global-mean}.
    96	\end{proof}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   100	  On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   101	  $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
   102	  h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
   103	  positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
   104	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
   105	    \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
   106	    =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   107	    \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	  It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
   110	  positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
   111	\end{proposition}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  The Fourier Laplacian $A = -\Delta$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$, being
   115	  multiplication by $|\xi|^2$ with its maximal domain. Multiplication $B_s =
   116	  -h_s$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm at most $M$. Thus, $H_s = A+B_s$ is
   117	  densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are
   118	  equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,
   119	  \[
   120	    H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).
   121	  \]
   122	  The first factor has a Neumann inverse because $\|B_s(A-ib)^{-1}\| \le M/b <
   123	  1$, and the same holds with $+ib$. To check self-adjointness directly, for $u
   124	  \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
   125	  \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,
   126	  $D(H_s^*) = D(H_s)$.
   127	
   128	  Set $c_{\mathrm{shift}} = 1+M$ and $J_s = H_s+c_{\mathrm{shift}} \ge 1$.
   129	  Integration by parts on $H^2$ gives
   130	  \[
   131	    \|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2=q_s(f)+c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_2^2,\qquad
   132	    \|f\|_{H^1}^2\le\|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2
   133	    \le c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_{H^1}^2.
   134	  \]

   136	  half-power norm; Fourier cutoffs give its density in $H^1$. Completion in the
   137	  equivalent norms identifies $D(J_s^{1/2})$ and $H^1$ as $L^2$ subspaces, since
   138	  both norms dominate $L^2$. This proves the stated form domain.

   140	  The spectral lower bound gives one direction of the Rayleigh identity. For the
   141	  reverse, nonzero spectral projections in $[E_s,E_s+\epsilon]$ give unit $H^2$
   142	  vectors with Rayleigh values at most $E_s+\epsilon$. The bottom is finite
   143	  because the operator is bounded below and has finite Rayleigh tests. Let
   144	  $\epsilon\downarrow0$. Real tests give the same infimum: $q_s(u+iv) =
   145	  q_s(u)+q_s(v)$, so the quotient is the norm-weighted average of the nonzero
   146	  real quotients. This proves the Rayleigh identity with $-E_s$ on the left. The
   147	  following negative upper bound justifies writing that value as
   148	  $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2$ in~\eqref{E:variational-real-rayleigh}.

   150	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial} supplies, for this original
   151	  $\Psi$, one unit compactly supported $w$ and a finite plateau mask with a
   152	  common strictly negative upper bound $\epsilon_0 > 0$. Its trial has support
   153	  in $B_{2L}$; choose its plateau radius $R_0 \ge 2L$. The unmasked form on this
   154	  same $w$ is no larger. Consequently, $-M \le E_s \le -\epsilon_0 < 0$, and

   156	  form tests gives $|E_s-E_t| \le \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty$ and therefore
   157	  \[
   158	    |\lambda_{\Psi,s}-\lambda_{\Psi,t}|
   159	    \le \frac{C_\Psi}{2\sqrt{\epsilon_0}}|s-t|.
   160	  \]

   162	  spectral theorem was applied to $H_s$. This proves
   163	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate}.

   167	
   168	\begin{proposition}[Monotone rates and the original point moment]
   169	  \label{P:variational-remove-mask}
   170	  There is an increasing family of admissible radial masks $m_R$ tending to one,
   171	  for which the compact ground rates satisfy
   172	  $\lambda_{R,s}\uparrow\lambda_{\Psi,s}$ uniformly on $I$ as $R \to \infty$,
   173	  with the compact ground statements used for $R \ge R_0(\Psi)$. For the
   174	  original canonical solution and any fixed $x$,
   175	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-unmasked-point-lower}
   176	    \liminf_{T\to\infty}T^{-\kappa}\log\E|u(T,x)|^2
   177	    \ge2I_\Psi-\frac{v_\Psi}{2}.
   178	  \end{equation}
   179	\end{proposition}
   180

181	\begin{proof}
   182	  Put $F(t) = e^{-1/t}$ for $t > 0$ and zero otherwise, and define
   183	  \[
   184	    \chi(r)=\frac{F(2-r)}{F(2-r)+F(r-1)},\qquad
   185	    m_R(x)=\chi(|x|/R).
   186	  \]
   187	  The denominator is positive. The numerator decreases and the second
   188	  denominator term increases; thus $\chi$ is nonincreasing, equals one on $r \le
   189	  1$, and zero on $r \ge 2$. Flatness of $F$ at zero gives smoothness. Since
   190	  $\chi$ is constant near zero, $m_R$ is smooth also at the spatial origin.
   191	  These even $[0,1]$ masks increase pointwise to one.
   192	
   193	  Choose $R_0$ so the preceding common trial lies in the plateau. Every $R \ge
   194	  R_0$ has the same negative margin. For each fixed $R$, the compact-family
   195	  theorem applies to $m_Rh_s$. Its real Rayleigh formula follows from the same
   196	  real/complex quotient argument as~\eqref{E:variational-real-rayleigh}. The
   197	  rates are continuous, positive, at most $\sqrt M$ and monotone in $R$. For
   198	  every fixed real unit $f \in H^1$, dominated convergence gives $\int m_Rh_sf^2
   199	  \to \int h_sf^2$. Hence,
   200	  \[
   201	    \sup_{R\ge R_0}\lambda_{R,s}^2
   202	    =\sup_{\|f\|_2=1,\ f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)}
   203	    \sup_{R\ge R_0}
   204	    \left(\int m_Rh_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right)
   205	    =\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2.
   206	  \]
   207	  Only two numerical suprema were interchanged. Positive square roots give the
   208	  pointwise rate convergence. For $R_n = R_0+n$ and $\epsilon > 0$, the
   209	  increasing open sets $\{s:\lambda_{\Psi,s}-\lambda_{R_n,s}<\epsilon\}$ cover
   210	  compact $I$. A finite subcover lies in the largest one, proving uniform
   211	  convergence. Monotonicity extends it to all real $R \to \infty$. Therefore,
   212	  $\int_I\lambda_{R,s}\ud s\uparrow I_\Psi$.
   213	
   214	  At each fixed $R$ use this very same mask in the operator path and mean when
   215	  applying Proposition~\ref{P:raw-block-original-lower}. It gives the lower
   216	  bound with $2\int_I\lambda_{R,s}\ud s-v_\Psi/2$ for the same original point
   217	  liminf. Taking the numerical supremum over these individual bounds proves
   218	  \eqref{E:variational-unmasked-point-lower}. There is no $R(T)$, unmasked noisy
   219	  wave, uniform-in-mask Gaussian estimate or exchange of source and time limits.
   220	  This proves Proposition~\ref{P:variational-remove-mask}.
   221	\end{proof}

   224	
   225	\begin{lemma}[Radon and Rayleigh dilation]\label{L:variational-control-dilation}
   226	  For $r > 0$ the map
   227	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-control-dilation}
   228	    (D_r\Psi)(s,x)=r^{d+2-\alpha}\Psi(s,rx)
   229	  \end{equation}
   230	  is a bijection of $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$, with inverse $D_{1/r}$. With
   231	  the same original covariance,
   232	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-dilation-values}
   233	    h_{D_r\Psi,s}(x)=r^2h_{\Psi,s}(rx),\qquad
   234	    v_{D_r\Psi}=r^{4-\alpha}v_\Psi,\qquad
   235	    \lambda_{D_r\Psi,s}=r\lambda_{\Psi,s},\quad
   236	    I_{D_r\Psi}=rI_\Psi.
   237	  \end{equation}
   238	\end{lemma}
   239	
   240	\begin{proof}
   241	  Positive dilation preserves the full smooth positive nonzero class;
   242	  multiplication of its amplitude powers gives the stated inverse. Homogeneity
   243	  of the physical Radon measure gives, for every nonnegative measurable $G$,
   244	  \[
   245	    \int G(ry)\Gamma(\ud y)
   246	    =r^{\alpha-d}\int G(z)\Gamma(\ud z).
   247	  \]
   248	  Indeed, its left pushforward measure on a Borel set $A$ is $\Gamma(A/r) =
   249	  r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$. Positive Tonelli applies this identity inside the
   250	  temporal convolution, giving $h_{D_r\Psi,s}(x) = r^2h_{\Psi,s}(rx)$. Now use
   251	  the \emph{Lebesgue} substitution $z = rx$ in the original pairing:
   252	  \[
   253	    v_{D_r\Psi}=r^{d+2-\alpha}r^2r^{-d}v_\Psi
   254	    =r^{4-\alpha}v_\Psi.
   255	  \]
   256	  This distinguishes the Radon pushforward from the spatial volume factor; it
   257	  includes singular covariances and white noise.
   258	
   259	  The map $U_rf(x) = r^{d/2}f(rx)$ is a unitary bijection on real $L^2$,
   260	  preserving $H^1,H^2$ as sets under its inverse. Weak derivatives give
   261	  $\|\nabla U_rf\|_2^2 = r^2\|\nabla f\|_2^2$ and $\int h_{D_r\Psi,s}(U_rf)^2 =
   262	  r^2\int h_{\Psi,s}f^2$. The real Rayleigh bijection proves the squared rate
   263	  identity; the rates are positive, so their square roots and integrals give
   264	  \eqref{E:variational-dilation-values}. On $H^2$ this is also $H_{D_r\Psi,s}U_r
   265	  = r^2U_rH_{\Psi,s}$. Time has not been rescaled. For compact masks the
   266	  corresponding identity uses $m_R(rx) = m_{R/r}(x)$; a fixed mask radius is not
   267	  invariant. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation}.
   268	\end{proof}

   270	\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic variational lower bounds]
   271	  \label{P:variational-positive-scores}
   272	  For $c > 0$, the set of variational values
   273	  $\{cI_\Psi-v_\Psi/2:\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}\}$ is nonempty and
   274	  bounded above. Its finite real supremum $S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is positive and
   275	  satisfies
   276	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-homogeneity}
   277	    S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}=c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}},
   278	    \qquad
   279	    Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}},
   280	  \end{equation}
   281	  where $Q_2$ is the original point liminf. The coefficient-one value is an
   282	  auxiliary variational value; no first-moment or source-constant identification
   283	  is asserted.
   284	\end{proposition}
   285	
   286	\begin{proof}
   287	  Write $k = 3-\alpha > 0$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $m = q/k > 1$. Fix one
   288	  $\Psi_0$ from the nonempty class and put $I_0 = I_{\Psi_0} > 0$, $v_0 =
   289	  v_{\Psi_0} > 0$. Positivity of the latter is
   290	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}. For $r_0 = (I_0/v_0)^{1/k} > 0$, which need
   291	  not be less than one, the exact real-power identity gives
   292	  \[
   293	    I_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}-v_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}/2
   294	    =r_0I_0-r_0^qv_0/2=r_0I_0/2>0.
   295	  \]
   296	  This positive value is obtained from a smooth nonnegative control.
   297	
   298	  For $c > 0$ put $r_c = c^{1/k}$ and $K_c = c^m > 0$.
   299	  Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation} and the exact scalar powers give,
   300	  for every $\Psi$,
   301	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-set-scaling}
   302	    cI_{D_{r_c}\Psi}-v_{D_{r_c}\Psi}/2
   303	    =K_c(I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2).
   304	  \end{equation}
   305	  Since $D_{r_c}$ is a bijection of the entire class, the whole set of
   306	  variational values with coefficient $c$ is $K_c$ times the whole
   307	  coefficient-one set of variational values.
   308	
   309	  We prove boundedness before taking finite-real suprema. The independent
   310	  Theorem~\ref{T:full-upper}, for the \emph{same canonical solution}, gives
   311	  \[
   312	    \E|u(T,0)|^2\le e(T+2)^d e^{C_{\mathrm{up}}T^\kappa},
   313	    \qquad T\ge1,\quad C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty.
   314	  \]
   315	  Its prefactor is negligible: choose $\epsilon = \kappa/2 > 0$, use $\log T \le
   316	  (T^\epsilon-1)/\epsilon$ and $\log(T+2) \le \log T+\log3$ for $T \ge 1$, and
   317	  divide by $T^\kappa$. Thus, the original point limsup is at most
   318	  $C_{\mathrm{up}}$. One fixed test/mask lower bound gives a finite lower bound
   319	  for $Q_2$, so $Q_2$ is finite. By~\eqref{E:variational-unmasked-point-lower}
   320	  every coefficient-two variational expression is at most this same $Q_2 \le
   321	  C_{\mathrm{up}}$, uniformly in $\Psi$.
   322	  Equation~\eqref{E:variational-score-set-scaling} at $c = 2$ consequently
   323	  bounds all coefficient-one variational values by $C_{\mathrm{up}}/K_2$. The
   324	  nonempty set has a finite real supremum $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} > 0$ by the
   325	  positive test above.
   326	
   327	  For general $c$, set equality and $K_c > 0$ show that $K_cS_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   328	  is the supremum: it is an upper bound, and every smaller number is exceeded by
   329	  $K_c$ times a coefficient-one variational expression within the corresponding
   330	  positive distance of its supremum. This proves finiteness, positivity and the
   331	  first identity in~\eqref{E:variational-score-homogeneity}. Taking the
   332	  numerical supremum of the coefficient-two lower bounds proves the second.
   333	  Although $2^m > 2$, the resulting $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}} > 2S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   334	  is only a comparison of auxiliary variational values. It is not a Jensen
   335	  improvement without a first-moment identification. This proves
   336	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
   337	\end{proof}

    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is

    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.

    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.

   253	/-- Every real Rayleigh value of a potential `V ≤ M` is at most `M`. -/
   254	theorem rayleighValue_le {V : Rd d → ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hVM : ∀ x, V x ≤ M) {q : ℝ}
   255	    (hq : q ∈ rayleighSet V) : q ≤ M := by

   257	  have h1 : ∫ x, V x * f x ^ 2 ≤ ∫ x, M * f x ^ 2 :=

   259	      fun x => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hVM x) (sq_nonneg _)
   260	  rw [integral_const_mul, hT.unit, mul_one] at h1
   261	  have h2 : 0 ≤ ∫ x, ‖g x‖ ^ 2 := integral_nonneg fun _ => sq_nonneg _
   262	  rw [rayleighValue]; linarith

   264	/-- Comparing identical unit tests: if `V - W ≤ D` pointwise, every trial of
   265	`V` is a trial of `W`, `R_V` is nonempty and `R_W` is bounded above, then
   266	`sup R_V ≤ sup R_W + D`. -/
   267	theorem sSup_rayleighSet_le_add {V W : Rd d → ℝ} {D : ℝ} (hD : ∀ x, V x - W x ≤ D)
   268	    (hW : ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, MemLp f 2 volume → Integrable (fun x => W x * f x ^ 2) volume)
   269	    (hne : (rayleighSet V).Nonempty) (hbdd : BddAbove (rayleighSet W)) :
   270	    sSup (rayleighSet V) ≤ sSup (rayleighSet W) + D := by
   271	  refine csSup_le hne fun q hq => ?_
   272	  obtain ⟨f, g, hT, rfl⟩ := hq
   273	  have hTW : IsRayleighTrial W f g := ⟨hT.memLp_f, hT.memLp_g, hT.weakGrad, hT.unit,
   274	    hW f hT.memLp_f⟩
   275	  have hmem : rayleighValue W f g ∈ rayleighSet W := ⟨f, g, hTW, rfl⟩
   276	  have hdiff : rayleighValue V f g - rayleighValue W f g ≤ D := by
   277	    have e : rayleighValue V f g - rayleighValue W f g = ∫ x, (V x - W x) * f x ^ 2 := by
   278	      rw [rayleighValue, rayleighValue]
   279	      simp_rw [sub_mul]
   280	      rw [integral_sub hT.integrable_pot hTW.integrable_pot]; ring
   281	    rw [e]
   282	    have hint : Integrable (fun x => (V x - W x) * f x ^ 2) volume := by
   283	      simp_rw [sub_mul]; exact hT.integrable_pot.sub hTW.integrable_pot
   284	    calc ∫ x, (V x - W x) * f x ^ 2 ≤ ∫ x, D * f x ^ 2 :=
   285	          integral_mono hint (hT.memLp_f.integrable_sq.const_mul D)
   286	            fun x => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hD x) (sq_nonneg _)
   287	      _ = D := by rw [integral_const_mul, hT.unit, mul_one]
   288	  linarith [le_csSup hbdd hmem]

   291	pointwise, both `V f²` and `W f²` are integrable for every `f ∈ L²`, and both
   292	value sets are nonempty and bounded above, then
   293	`|sup R_V - sup R_W| ≤ D` (TeX line 156, "comparing identical unit form
   294	tests"). -/
   295	theorem abs_sSup_rayleighSet_sub_le {V W : Rd d → ℝ} {D : ℝ} (hD : ∀ x, |V x - W x| ≤ D)
   296	    (hV : ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, MemLp f 2 volume → Integrable (fun x => V x * f x ^ 2) volume)
   297	    (hW : ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, MemLp f 2 volume → Integrable (fun x => W x * f x ^ 2) volume)
   298	    (hneV : (rayleighSet V).Nonempty) (hneW : (rayleighSet W).Nonempty)
   299	    (hbV : BddAbove (rayleighSet V)) (hbW : BddAbove (rayleighSet W)) :
   300	    |sSup (rayleighSet V) - sSup (rayleighSet W)| ≤ D := by
   301	  have h1 := sSup_rayleighSet_le_add (fun x => (le_abs_self _).trans (hD x)) hW hneV hbW
   302	  have h2 := sSup_rayleighSet_le_add (D := D) (fun x => by
   303	    have := hD x; rw [abs_sub_comm] at this; exact (le_abs_self _).trans this) hV hneW hbV
   304	  rw [abs_le]; constructor <;> linarith

   306	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `|√a - √b| ≤ |a - b|/(2√ε)` for
   307	`a, b ≥ ε > 0`. -/
   308	theorem abs_sqrt_sub_le {ε a b : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ha : ε ≤ a) (hb : ε ≤ b) :
   309	    |Real.sqrt a - Real.sqrt b| ≤ |a - b| / (2 * Real.sqrt ε) := by
   310	  have hse : 0 < Real.sqrt ε := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hε
   311	  have hsa : Real.sqrt ε ≤ Real.sqrt a := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt ha
   312	  have hsb : Real.sqrt ε ≤ Real.sqrt b := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hb
   313	  have hprod : (Real.sqrt a - Real.sqrt b) * (Real.sqrt a + Real.sqrt b) = a - b := by
   314	    have e1 := Real.sq_sqrt (hε.le.trans ha)
   315	    have e2 := Real.sq_sqrt (hε.le.trans hb)
   316	    nlinarith
   317	  rw [le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
   318	  have hsum : 2 * Real.sqrt ε ≤ Real.sqrt a + Real.sqrt b := by linarith
   319	  calc |Real.sqrt a - Real.sqrt b| * (2 * Real.sqrt ε)
   320	      ≤ |Real.sqrt a - Real.sqrt b| * (Real.sqrt a + Real.sqrt b) :=
   321	        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsum (abs_nonneg _)
   322	    _ = |a - b| := by
   323	        rw [← hprod, abs_mul, abs_of_pos (show 0 < Real.sqrt a + Real.sqrt b by linarith)]

   327	/-- **`P:variational-unmasked-rate`, Rayleigh-form part, general form.**  For
   328	tempered `Γ`, `μ` with the spectral convention, `Γ` nonzero and locally
   329	finite with the set scaling of `H:homog`, `α < 2`, `0 ≤ a < 1` and
   330	`Ψ ∈ CPos`: there are reals `ε > 0`, `M ≥ ε`, `C ≥ 0` such that, for
   331	`s, t ∈ [0,1]`, `0 ≤ h_s ≤ M`, `|h_s(x) - h_t(x)| ≤ C|s - t|`, the real
   332	Rayleigh value set `R_s` of `h_s` is nonempty and bounded above with
   333	`ε ≤ sup R_s ≤ M` (a uniform positive floor), `λ_s² = sup R_s`,
   334	`√ε ≤ λ_s ≤ √M`, `|sup R_s - sup R_t| ≤ C|s - t|`,
   335	`|λ_s - λ_t| ≤ C/(2√ε) |s - t|`, `λ` is integrable on `(0,1)`, and
   336	`√ε ≤ I_Ψ ≤ √M` (so `I_Ψ` is positive and finite). -/
   337	theorem unmasked_rate {alpha : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓt : IsTempered Γ)
   338	    (hμt : IsTempered μ) (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ]
   339	    (hS : SetScaling alpha Γ) (hα : alpha < 2) (hΓ : Γ ≠ 0) {a : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha : a < 1)
   340	    {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Ψ ∈ CPos d) :
   341	    ∃ ε M C : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε ≤ M ∧ 0 ≤ C ∧
   342	      (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x, 0 ≤ mean a Γ Ψ s x ∧ mean a Γ Ψ s x ≤ M) ∧
   343	      (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x,
   344	        |mean a Γ Ψ s x - mean a Γ Ψ t x| ≤ C * |s - t|) ∧
   345	      (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
   346	        (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)).Nonempty ∧ BddAbove (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)) ∧
   347	        ε ≤ sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)) ∧ sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)) ≤ M ∧
   348	        rate a Γ Ψ s ^ 2 = sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)) ∧
   349	        Real.sqrt ε ≤ rate a Γ Ψ s ∧ rate a Γ Ψ s ≤ Real.sqrt M) ∧
   350	      (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
   351	        |sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)) - sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ t))| ≤
   352	          C * |s - t|) ∧
   353	      (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
   354	        |rate a Γ Ψ s - rate a Γ Ψ t| ≤ C / (2 * Real.sqrt ε) * |s - t|) ∧
   355	      IntegrableOn (rate a Γ Ψ) (Ioo 0 1) ∧
   356	      Real.sqrt ε ≤ integratedRate a Γ Ψ ∧ integratedRate a Γ Ψ ≤ Real.sqrt M := by
   357	  obtain ⟨M, C, hM0, hC, -, -, hbd, hlip⟩ := global_mean hΓt hμt hsp hΨ ha
   358	  have hcont : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, Continuous (mean a Γ Ψ s) := fun s hs =>
   359	    mean_continuous_of_lip hC fun x x' => hlip s hs s hs x x'
   360	  have hpot : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, MemLp f 2 volume →
   361	      Integrable (fun x => mean a Γ Ψ s x * f x ^ 2) volume := fun s hs f hf =>
   362	    integrable_pot_of_bounded (hcont s hs) (M := M) (fun x => by
   363	      rw [abs_of_nonneg (hbd s hs x).1]; exact (hbd s hs x).2) hf
   364	  have hlipx : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x,
   365	      |mean a Γ Ψ s x - mean a Γ Ψ t x| ≤ C * |s - t| := fun s hs t ht x => by
   366	    rw [← dist_same_space s t x]; exact hlip s hs t ht x x
   367	  obtain ⟨hzc, hz0, hzs, σ₀, x₀, -, -, hzpos⟩ := psiBar_data hΨ
   368	  have hzne : psiBar Ψ ≠ 0 := fun h => by rw [h] at hzpos; exact lt_irrefl _ hzpos
   369	  obtain ⟨f, g, ε, hε, -, hf, hg, hw, hu, hval⟩ :=
   370	    dilation_floor hS hα hΓ hzc hzs hz0 hzne (psiBar_conv_integrable hΓt hμt hsp hΨ)
   371	  have hT : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, IsRayleighTrial (mean a Γ Ψ s) f g := fun s hs =>
   372	    ⟨hf, hg, hw, hu, hpot s hs f hf⟩
   373	  have hmem : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, rayleighValue (mean a Γ Ψ s) f g ∈
   374	      rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s) := fun s hs => ⟨f, g, hT s hs, rfl⟩
   375	  have hvε : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ε ≤ rayleighValue (mean a Γ Ψ s) f g := fun s hs =>
   376	    hval _ (conv_psiBar_le_mean hΓt hμt hsp hΨ ha0 ha hs) (hpot s hs f hf)
   377	  have hne : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)).Nonempty := fun s hs =>
   378	    ⟨_, hmem s hs⟩
   379	  have hbdd : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, BddAbove (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)) := fun s hs =>
   380	    ⟨M, fun q hq => rayleighValue_le (fun x => (hbd s hs x).2) hq⟩
   381	  have hlo : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ε ≤ sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)) := fun s hs =>
   382	    (hvε s hs).trans (le_csSup (hbdd s hs) (hmem s hs))
   383	  have hhi : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)) ≤ M := fun s hs =>
   384	    csSup_le (hne s hs) fun q hq => rayleighValue_le (fun x => (hbd s hs x).2) hq
   385	  have h0 : (0 : ℝ) ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 := ⟨le_rfl, zero_le_one⟩
   386	  have hεM : ε ≤ M := (hlo 0 h0).trans (hhi 0 h0)
   387	  have hrate : ∀ s, rate a Γ Ψ s = Real.sqrt (sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s))) :=
   388	    fun s => rfl
   389	  have hsupLip : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
   390	      |sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ s)) - sSup (rayleighSet (mean a Γ Ψ t))| ≤
   391	        C * |s - t| := fun s hs t ht =>
   392	    abs_sSup_rayleighSet_sub_le (hlipx s hs t ht) (hpot s hs) (hpot t ht) (hne s hs)
   393	      (hne t ht) (hbdd s hs) (hbdd t ht)
   394	  have hrateLip : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
   395	      |rate a Γ Ψ s - rate a Γ Ψ t| ≤ C / (2 * Real.sqrt ε) * |s - t| := by
   396	    intro s hs t ht
   397	    rw [hrate, hrate]
   398	    refine (abs_sqrt_sub_le hε (hlo s hs) (hlo t ht)).trans ?_
   399	    rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, mul_comm C]
   400	    exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (by rw [mul_comm]; exact hsupLip s hs t ht)
   401	      (by positivity)
   402	  have hrateLo : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, Real.sqrt ε ≤ rate a Γ Ψ s := fun s hs => by
   403	    rw [hrate]; exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (hlo s hs)
   404	  have hrateHi : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, rate a Γ Ψ s ≤ Real.sqrt M := fun s hs => by
   405	    rw [hrate]; exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (hhi s hs)
   406	  have hcontOn : ContinuousOn (rate a Γ Ψ) (Icc 0 1) := by
   407	    refine (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul
   408	      (K := Real.toNNReal (C / (2 * Real.sqrt ε))) fun s hs t ht => ?_).continuousOn
   409	    rw [Real.dist_eq, Real.dist_eq, Real.coe_toNNReal _ (by positivity)]
   410	    exact hrateLip s hs t ht
   411	  have hint : IntegrableOn (rate a Γ Ψ) (Ioo 0 1) :=
   412	    (hcontOn.integrableOn_compact isCompact_Icc).mono_set Ioo_subset_Icc_self
   413	  have hvol : (volume : Measure ℝ).real (Ioo 0 1) = 1 := by simp
   414	  refine ⟨ε, M, C, hε, hεM, hC, hbd, hlipx, fun s hs => ⟨hne s hs, hbdd s hs, hlo s hs,
   415	    hhi s hs, ?_, hrateLo s hs, hrateHi s hs⟩, hsupLip, hrateLip, hint, ?_, ?_⟩
   416	  · rw [hrate]; exact Real.sq_sqrt (hε.le.trans (hlo s hs))
   417	  · have := setIntegral_mono_on (integrableOn_const (C := Real.sqrt ε) (by simp)) hint
   418	      measurableSet_Ioo fun s hs => hrateLo s (Ioo_subset_Icc_self hs)
   419	    rwa [setIntegral_const, hvol, one_smul] at this
   420	  · have := setIntegral_mono_on hint (integrableOn_const (C := Real.sqrt M) (by simp))
   421	      measurableSet_Ioo fun s hs => hrateHi s (Ioo_subset_Icc_self hs)
   422	    rwa [setIntegral_const, hvol, one_smul] at this

   428	`G(σ, x) = Ψ(σ, x) h_σ(x)` on `ℝ × ℝ^d`. -/
   429	def costIntegrand (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) (p : ℝ × Rd d) : ℝ :=
   430	  Ψ p * mean a Γ Ψ p.1 p.2

   432	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: for tempered `Γ`, `μ` with the spectral
   433	convention, `a < 1` and `Ψ ∈ CPos`, the variance integrand is continuous with
   434	compact support (joint Lipschitz bound of the mean on `[0,1] × ℝ^d`, and
   435	`tsupport Ψ ⊆ (0,1) × ℝ^d`). -/
   436	theorem costIntegrand_data {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓt : IsTempered Γ) (hμt : IsTempered μ)
   437	    (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ) {a : ℝ} (ha : a < 1) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ}
   438	    (hΨ : Ψ ∈ CPos d) :
   439	    Continuous (costIntegrand a Γ Ψ) ∧ HasCompactSupport (costIntegrand a Γ Ψ) := by
   440	  obtain ⟨M, C, -, hC, -, -, -, hlip⟩ := global_mean hΓt hμt hsp hΨ ha
   441	  have hmc : ContinuousOn (fun p : ℝ × Rd d => mean a Γ Ψ p.1 p.2) (Icc 0 1 ×ˢ univ) := by
   442	    refine (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul (K := Real.toNNReal C)
   443	      fun p hp q hq => ?_).continuousOn
   444	    rw [Real.dist_eq, Real.coe_toNNReal _ hC]
   445	    exact hlip p.1 hp.1 q.1 hq.1 p.2 q.2
   446	  have hGc : ContinuousOn (costIntegrand a Γ Ψ) (Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ univ) :=
   447	    hΨ.1.continuous.continuousOn.mul
   448	      (hmc.mono (prod_mono Ioo_subset_Icc_self subset_rfl))
   449	  refine ⟨hGc.continuous_of_tsupport_subset (isOpen_Ioo.prod isOpen_univ)
   450	    ((tsupport_mul_subset_left).trans hΨ.2.2.1), hΨ.2.1.mul_right⟩

   452	/-- `v_Ψ` (`VariationalDilation.rawCost`, the integral form of
   453	`E:compact-raw-cost`) is a genuine integral: for tempered `Γ`, `μ` with the
   454	spectral convention, `a < 1` and `Ψ ∈ CPos`, every spatial integrand
   455	`x ↦ Ψ(σ,x) h_σ(x)` is integrable, the time integrand
   456	`σ ↦ ∫ Ψ(σ,x) h_σ(x) dx` is integrable on `(0,1)`, and `v_Ψ` equals the
   457	integral of `Ψ(σ,x) h_σ(x)` over `ℝ × ℝ^d`. -/

   459	    (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ) {a : ℝ} (ha : a < 1) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ}
   460	    (hΨ : Ψ ∈ CPos d) :
   461	    (∀ σ, Integrable (fun x => Ψ (σ, x) * mean a Γ Ψ σ x) volume) ∧
   462	      IntegrableOn (fun σ => ∫ x, Ψ (σ, x) * mean a Γ Ψ σ x) (Ioo 0 1) ∧
   463	      rawCost a Γ Ψ = ∫ p, costIntegrand a Γ Ψ p := by
   464	  obtain ⟨hGc, hGs⟩ := costIntegrand_data hΓt hμt hsp ha hΨ
   465	  have hGi : Integrable (costIntegrand a Γ Ψ) (volume.prod volume) := by
   466	    rw [← Measure.volume_eq_prod]; exact hGc.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hGs
   467	  obtain ⟨B, L, R, -, -, -, -, hR⟩ := ctrl_data hΨ
   468	  refine ⟨fun σ => ?_, (hGi.integral_prod_left).integrableOn, ?_⟩
   469	  · have hc : Continuous fun x => costIntegrand a Γ Ψ (σ, x) := hGc.comp (by fun_prop)
   470	    have hs : HasCompactSupport fun x => costIntegrand a Γ Ψ (σ, x) := by
   471	      refine HasCompactSupport.intro (isCompact_closedBall (0 : Rd d) R) fun z hz => ?_
   472	      rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right, not_le] at hz
   473	      simp [costIntegrand, hR σ z hz]
   474	    exact hc.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hs
   475	  · rw [rawCost, setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, Measure.volume_eq_prod,
   476	      integral_prod _ hGi]
   477	    · rfl
   478	    · intro σ hσ
   479	      simp [VariationalMean.eq_zero_of_time hΨ.2.2.1 hσ]

   481	/-- `v_Ψ > 0`: under the hypotheses of `unmasked_rate`, the variance of every

    14	Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces and no weak derivatives, so this foundation is

    21	  `‖∇f‖₂² = ∫ ‖g‖²` does not depend on the choice of `g`.  This justifies

    25	`∫ V f² - ∫ ‖g‖²` over `f ∈ H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)` with `‖f‖₂ = 1` and weak gradient

    62	/-! ### Test functions, weak gradients and `H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)` -/
    63	
    64	/-- `φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d; ℝ)`: smooth with compact support. -/
    65	def IsTestFunction (φ : Rd d → ℝ) : Prop :=
    66	  ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ
    67	
    68	/-- `g` is a weak gradient of `f`: for every test function `φ` and every
    69	direction `v`, `∫ f ∂_v φ = -∫ ⟪g, v⟫ φ`. -/
    70	def HasWeakGradient (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) : Prop :=
    71	  ∀ φ : Rd d → ℝ, IsTestFunction φ → ∀ v : Rd d,
    72	    ∫ x, f x * fderiv ℝ φ x v = -∫ x, inner ℝ (g x) v * φ x
    73	
    74	/-- The real Sobolev space `H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)`: `f ∈ L^2` with a weak gradient in
    75	`L^2`. -/
    76	def MemH1 (f : Rd d → ℝ) : Prop :=
    77	  MemLp f 2 volume ∧ ∃ g : Rd d → Rd d, MemLp g 2 volume ∧ HasWeakGradient f g
    78	
    79	/-- An `L^2` weak gradient is unique almost everywhere. -/
    80	theorem weakGradient_ae_unique {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g₁ g₂ : Rd d → Rd d}
    81	    (h₁ : HasWeakGradient f g₁) (h₂ : HasWeakGradient f g₂)
    82	    (hg₁ : MemLp g₁ 2 volume) (hg₂ : MemLp g₂ 2 volume) :
    83	    g₁ =ᵐ[volume] g₂ := by
    84	  have hloc : ∀ (g : Rd d → Rd d), MemLp g 2 volume → ∀ v : Rd d,
    85	      LocallyIntegrable (fun x => inner ℝ (g x) v) volume := by
    86	    intro g hg v
    87	    have : MemLp (fun x => inner ℝ (g x) v) 2 volume := by
    88	      have := (innerSL ℝ v).comp_memLp' hg
    89	      refine this.congr_norm ?_ (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_)
    90	      · exact hg.aestronglyMeasurable.inner_const
    91	      · simp [real_inner_comm]
    92	    exact this.locallyIntegrable (by norm_num)
    93	  have hcoord : ∀ v : Rd d, ∀ᵐ x ∂volume, inner ℝ (g₁ x - g₂ x) v = 0 := by
    94	    intro v
    95	    have hL : LocallyIntegrable (fun x => inner ℝ (g₁ x - g₂ x) v) volume := by
    96	      simp_rw [inner_sub_left]
    97	      exact (hloc g₁ hg₁ v).sub (hloc g₂ hg₂ v)
    98	    refine ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero hL ?_
    99	    intro φ hφ hφc
   100	    have i₁ : Integrable (fun x => φ x • inner ℝ (g₁ x) v) volume :=
   101	      (hloc g₁ hg₁ v).integrable_smul_left_of_hasCompactSupport hφ.continuous hφc
   102	    have i₂ : Integrable (fun x => φ x • inner ℝ (g₂ x) v) volume :=
   103	      (hloc g₂ hg₂ v).integrable_smul_left_of_hasCompactSupport hφ.continuous hφc
   104	    have e₁ := h₁ φ ⟨hφ, hφc⟩ v
   105	    have e₂ := h₂ φ ⟨hφ, hφc⟩ v
   106	    have : ∀ x, φ x • inner ℝ (g₁ x - g₂ x) v =
   107	        φ x • inner ℝ (g₁ x) v - φ x • inner ℝ (g₂ x) v := by
   108	      intro x; rw [inner_sub_left, smul_sub]
   109	    simp_rw [this]
   110	    rw [integral_sub i₁ i₂]
   111	    simp only [smul_eq_mul] at *
   112	    have c₁ : ∫ x, φ x * inner ℝ (g₁ x) v = ∫ x, inner ℝ (g₁ x) v * φ x := by
   113	      congr 1; funext x; ring
   114	    have c₂ : ∫ x, φ x * inner ℝ (g₂ x) v = ∫ x, inner ℝ (g₂ x) v * φ x := by
   115	      congr 1; funext x; ring
   116	    rw [c₁, c₂]
   117	    linarith
   118	  have hall : ∀ᵐ x ∂volume, ∀ i : Fin d,
   119	      inner ℝ (g₁ x - g₂ x) (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = 0 :=
   120	    ae_all_iff.mpr fun i => hcoord _
   121	  filter_upwards [hall] with x hx
   122	  have : g₁ x - g₂ x = 0 := by
   123	    ext i
   124	    have := hx i
   125	    rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_single_right] at this
   126	    simpa using this
   127	  exact sub_eq_zero.mp this

   129	/-! ### The `L^2` dilation `U_r` -/
   130	
   131	/-- `U_r f(x) = r^{d/2} f(r x)` (TeX line 260), for real- or vector-valued `f`. -/
   132	def dilL2 {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   133	    (r : ℝ) (f : Rd d → E) : Rd d → E :=
   134	  fun x => r ^ ((d : ℝ) / 2) • f (r • x)
   135	
   136	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `(r^{d/2})² = r^d`. -/
   137	theorem rpow_half_sq {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) : (r ^ ((d : ℝ) / 2)) ^ 2 = r ^ d := by
   138	  rw [← Real.rpow_natCast (r ^ ((d : ℝ) / 2)) 2, ← Real.rpow_mul hr.le,
   139	    ← Real.rpow_natCast r d]
   140	  congr 1; push_cast; ring
   141	
   142	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: Lebesgue substitution `y = r x`,
   143	`∫ r^d G(r x) dx = ∫ G` (unconditional). -/
   144	theorem integral_jacobian {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   145	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (G : Rd d → E) :
   146	    ∫ x, (r ^ d : ℝ) • G (r • x) = ∫ y, G y := by
   147	  rw [integral_smul, Measure.integral_comp_smul_of_nonneg volume G r (hR := hr.le),
   148	    finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ (by positivity), one_smul]
   149	
   150	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: integrability is invariant under the
   151	substitution `y = r x`. -/
   152	theorem integrable_jacobian_iff {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   153	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (G : Rd d → E) :
   154	    Integrable (fun x => (r ^ d : ℝ) • G (r • x)) volume ↔ Integrable G volume := by
   155	  have e : (fun x => (r ^ d : ℝ) • G (r • x)) = (r ^ d : ℝ) • (fun x => G (r • x)) := rfl
   156	  rw [e, integrable_smul_iff (by positivity : (r ^ d : ℝ) ≠ 0),
   157	    integrable_comp_smul_iff volume G hr.ne']
   158	
   159	/-- `U_r` maps `L^2` into `L^2`. -/
   160	theorem memLp_dilL2 {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   161	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {f : Rd d → E} (hf : MemLp f 2 volume) :
   162	    MemLp (dilL2 r f) 2 volume := by
   163	  have hm : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => f (r • x)) volume :=
   164	    hf.aestronglyMeasurable.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving (Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_smul volume hr.ne')
   165	  have : MemLp (fun x => f (r • x)) 2 volume := by
   166	    rw [memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm hm]
   167	    rw [memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm hf.aestronglyMeasurable] at hf
   168	    exact (integrable_comp_smul_iff volume (fun y => ‖f y‖ ^ 2) hr.ne').mpr hf
   169	  exact this.const_smul _
   170	
   171	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `‖U_r f(x)‖² = r^d ‖f(r x)‖²`. -/
   172	theorem norm_dilL2_sq {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   173	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (f : Rd d → E) (x : Rd d) :
   174	    ‖dilL2 r f x‖ ^ 2 = (r ^ d : ℝ) • ‖f (r • x)‖ ^ 2 := by
   175	  rw [dilL2, norm_smul, mul_pow, Real.norm_of_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hr.le _),
   176	    rpow_half_sq hr, smul_eq_mul]
   177	
   178	/-- `U_r` preserves the `L^2` norm: `∫ ‖U_r f‖² = ∫ ‖f‖²`. -/
   179	theorem integral_norm_dilL2_sq {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   180	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (f : Rd d → E) :

181	    ∫ x, ‖dilL2 r f x‖ ^ 2 = ∫ x, ‖f x‖ ^ 2 := by
   182	  simp_rw [norm_dilL2_sq hr]
   183	  exact integral_jacobian hr (fun y => ‖f y‖ ^ 2)
   184	
   185	/-- `U_r` transports weak gradients: if `g` is a weak gradient of `f`, then
   186	`r U_r g` is a weak gradient of `U_r f` (TeX line 262,
   187	`‖∇U_r f‖₂² = r² ‖∇f‖₂²`). -/
   188	theorem hasWeakGradient_dilL2 {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d}
   189	    (h : HasWeakGradient f g) :
   190	    HasWeakGradient (dilL2 r f) (fun x => r • dilL2 r g x) := by
   191	  intro φ hφ v
   192	  set ψ : Rd d → ℝ := fun y => φ (r⁻¹ • y) with hψdef
   193	  have hψ : IsTestFunction ψ :=
   194	    ⟨hφ.1.comp (contDiff_const_smul r⁻¹), hφ.2.comp_smul (inv_ne_zero hr.ne')⟩
   195	  have hφψ : φ = fun x => ψ (r • x) := by
   196	    funext x; simp [hψdef, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hr.ne']
   197	  have hD : ∀ x, fderiv ℝ φ x v = r * fderiv ℝ ψ (r • x) v := by
   198	    intro x; rw [hφψ, fderiv_comp_smul]; rfl
   199	  have hL : ∀ x, dilL2 r f x * fderiv ℝ φ x v =
   200	      (r ^ ((d : ℝ) / 2) * r / r ^ d) *
   201	        ((r ^ d : ℝ) • (f (r • x) * fderiv ℝ ψ (r • x) v)) := by
   202	    intro x
   203	    rw [hD, dilL2, smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul]
   204	    field_simp
   205	  have hR : ∀ x, inner ℝ (r • dilL2 r g x) v * φ x =
   206	      (r ^ ((d : ℝ) / 2) * r / r ^ d) *
   207	        ((r ^ d : ℝ) • (inner ℝ (g (r • x)) v * ψ (r • x))) := by
   208	    intro x
   209	    rw [hφψ, dilL2, real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_left, smul_eq_mul]
   210	    field_simp
   211	  simp_rw [hL, hR]
   212	  rw [integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul,
   213	    integral_jacobian hr (fun y => f y * fderiv ℝ ψ y v),
   214	    integral_jacobian hr (fun y => inner ℝ (g y) v * ψ y), h ψ hψ v]
   215	  ring
   216	
   217	/-! ### The real Rayleigh set of `E:variational-real-rayleigh` -/
   218	
   219	/-- A trial of the real Rayleigh supremum for the potential `V`: `f ∈ L^2`
   220	with `L^2` weak gradient `g` (so `f ∈ H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)`), `‖f‖₂ = 1`, and
   221	`V f²` integrable (explicit side condition, see the module doc). -/
   222	structure IsRayleighTrial (V : Rd d → ℝ) (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) : Prop where
   223	  memLp_f : MemLp f 2 volume
   224	  memLp_g : MemLp g 2 volume
   225	  weakGrad : HasWeakGradient f g
   226	  unit : ∫ x, f x ^ 2 = 1
   227	  integrable_pot : Integrable (fun x => V x * f x ^ 2) volume
   228	
   229	/-- The Rayleigh value `∫ V f² - ‖∇f‖₂²`. -/
   230	def rayleighValue (V : Rd d → ℝ) (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) : ℝ :=
   231	  (∫ x, V x * f x ^ 2) - ∫ x, ‖g x‖ ^ 2
   232	
   233	/-- The set of real Rayleigh values over unit `f ∈ H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)`; its
   234	supremum is the right side of `E:variational-real-rayleigh`. -/
   235	def rayleighSet (V : Rd d → ℝ) : Set ℝ :=
   236	  {q | ∃ f g, IsRayleighTrial V f g ∧ rayleighValue V f g = q}
   237	
   238	/-- The rate attached to a potential: `√(sup of the real Rayleigh values)`.
   239	For `V = h_{Ψ,s}` this is the manuscript's `λ_{Ψ,s}` through
   240	`E:variational-real-rayleigh` (see `VariationalDilation`). -/
   241	def rayleighRate (V : Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   242	  Real.sqrt (sSup (rayleighSet V))
   243	
   244	/-- Every trial `f` lies in `H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)`. -/
   245	theorem IsRayleighTrial.memH1 {V : Rd d → ℝ} {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d}
   246	    (h : IsRayleighTrial V f g) : MemH1 f :=
   247	  ⟨h.memLp_f, g, h.memLp_g, h.weakGrad⟩
   248	
   249	/-- The Rayleigh value of a trial depends only on `f` (uniqueness of the weak
   250	gradient), so the set over pairs is the set over `f ∈ H^1`. -/
   251	theorem rayleighValue_indep {V : Rd d → ℝ} {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g₁ g₂ : Rd d → Rd d}
   252	    (h₁ : IsRayleighTrial V f g₁) (h₂ : IsRayleighTrial V f g₂) :
   253	    rayleighValue V f g₁ = rayleighValue V f g₂ := by
   254	  have := weakGradient_ae_unique h₁.weakGrad h₂.weakGrad h₁.memLp_g h₂.memLp_g
   255	  unfold rayleighValue
   256	  congr 1
   257	  exact integral_congr_ae (this.mono fun x hx => by simp only [hx])
   258	
   259	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: a trial for `V` dilates to a trial for
   260	`r² V(r ·)` with `r²` times the value. -/
   261	theorem IsRayleighTrial.dil {V : Rd d → ℝ} {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d}
   262	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (h : IsRayleighTrial V f g) :
   263	    IsRayleighTrial (fun x => r ^ 2 * V (r • x)) (dilL2 r f) (fun x => r • dilL2 r g x) ∧
   264	      rayleighValue (fun x => r ^ 2 * V (r • x)) (dilL2 r f) (fun x => r • dilL2 r g x) =
   265	        r ^ 2 * rayleighValue V f g := by
   266	  have hpot : ∀ x, r ^ 2 * V (r • x) * dilL2 r f x ^ 2 =
   267	      r ^ 2 * ((r ^ d : ℝ) • (V (r • x) * f (r • x) ^ 2)) := by
   268	    intro x
   269	    have := norm_dilL2_sq hr f x
   270	    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs, sq_abs] at this
   271	    rw [this, smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul]; ring
   272	  have hgrad : ∀ x, ‖r • dilL2 r g x‖ ^ 2 = r ^ 2 * ((r ^ d : ℝ) • ‖g (r • x)‖ ^ 2) := by
   273	    intro x
   274	    rw [norm_smul, mul_pow, Real.norm_of_nonneg hr.le, norm_dilL2_sq hr]
   275	  have hsq : ∀ x, dilL2 r f x ^ 2 = (r ^ d : ℝ) • f (r • x) ^ 2 := by
   276	    intro x
   277	    have := norm_dilL2_sq hr f x
   278	    rwa [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs, sq_abs] at this
   279	  refine ⟨⟨memLp_dilL2 hr h.memLp_f, (memLp_dilL2 hr h.memLp_g).const_smul r,
   280	    hasWeakGradient_dilL2 hr h.weakGrad, ?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
   281	  · simp_rw [hsq]; rw [integral_jacobian hr (fun y => f y ^ 2)]; exact h.unit
   282	  · simp_rw [hpot]
   283	    exact ((integrable_jacobian_iff hr (fun y => V y * f y ^ 2)).mpr
   284	      h.integrable_pot).const_mul _
   285	  · unfold rayleighValue
   286	    simp_rw [hpot, hgrad]
   287	    rw [integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul, integral_jacobian hr (fun y => V y * f y ^ 2),
   288	      integral_jacobian hr (fun y => ‖g y‖ ^ 2)]
   289	    ring
   290	
   291	/-- The real Rayleigh bijection (TeX lines 260-264):
   292	`rayleighSet (r² V(r ·)) = r² · rayleighSet V` for every real potential `V`
   293	and `r > 0`. -/
   294	theorem rayleighSet_dil (V : Rd d → ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   295	    rayleighSet (fun x => r ^ 2 * V (r • x)) = (r ^ 2) • rayleighSet V := by
   296	  ext q
   297	  constructor
   298	  · rintro ⟨F, G, hT, rfl⟩
   299	    have hri : 0 < r⁻¹ := inv_pos.mpr hr
   300	    obtain ⟨hT', hv'⟩ := hT.dil hri
   301	    have hV : (fun x => r⁻¹ ^ 2 * (r ^ 2 * V (r • r⁻¹ • x))) = V := by
   302	      funext x
   303	      rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_smul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_pow,
   304	        inv_mul_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_pow, one_mul]
   305	    rw [hV] at hT' hv'
   306	    refine Set.mem_smul_set.mpr ⟨_, ⟨_, _, hT', rfl⟩, ?_⟩
   307	    rw [hv', smul_eq_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_pow, mul_inv_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_pow, one_mul]
   308	  · rintro ⟨_, ⟨f, g, hT, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
   309	    obtain ⟨hT', hv'⟩ := hT.dil hr
   310	    exact ⟨_, _, hT', hv'⟩
   311	
   312	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `√(sSup (r² S)) = r √(sSup S)` for every
   313	set `S` of reals and `r > 0` (no boundedness or nonemptiness needed). -/
   314	theorem sqrt_sSup_scale (S : Set ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   315	    Real.sqrt (sSup ((r ^ 2) • S)) = r * Real.sqrt (sSup S) := by
   316	  rw [Real.sSup_smul_of_nonneg (by positivity), smul_eq_mul, Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity),
   317	    Real.sqrt_sq hr.le]
   318	
   319	/-- The squared-rate identity: `sup R(r² V(r ·)) = r² sup R(V)`. -/
   320	theorem sSup_rayleighSet_dil (V : Rd d → ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   321	    sSup (rayleighSet (fun x => r ^ 2 * V (r • x))) = r ^ 2 * sSup (rayleighSet V) := by
   322	  rw [rayleighSet_dil V hr, Real.sSup_smul_of_nonneg (by positivity), smul_eq_mul]

   324	/-- The rate identity: `rayleighRate (r² V(r ·)) = r · rayleighRate V`. -/

    90	/-! ### The control class and the dilation -/
    91	
    92	/-- `E:variational-positive-class`: nonnegative, nonzero
    93	`Ψ ∈ C_c^∞((0,1) × ℝ^d; ℝ)`, as smooth functions on `ℝ × ℝ^d` with compact
    94	support inside `(0,1) × ℝ^d`. -/
    95	def CPos (d : ℕ) : Set (ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) :=
    96	  {Ψ | ContDiff ℝ ∞ Ψ ∧ HasCompactSupport Ψ ∧
    97	    tsupport Ψ ⊆ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Set.univ ∧ (∀ p, 0 ≤ Ψ p) ∧ Ψ ≠ 0}
    98	
    99	/-- `E:variational-control-dilation`: `(D_r Ψ)(s,x) = r^{d+2-α} Ψ(s, r x)`. -/
   100	def dil (alpha r : ℝ) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ :=
   101	  fun p => r ^ ((d : ℝ) + 2 - alpha) * Ψ (p.1, r • p.2)
   102	
   103	/-- The class `CPos` is nonempty (TeX lines 13-17; here a smooth bump on
   104	`ℝ × ℝ^d` centred at `(1/2, 0)` with outer radius `1/4` replaces the
   105	manuscript's explicit product of `e^{-1/(1-z²)}` bumps). -/
   106	theorem CPos_nonempty (d : ℕ) : (CPos d).Nonempty := by
   107	  let b : ContDiffBump ((1 / 2 : ℝ), (0 : Rd d)) := ⟨1 / 8, 1 / 4, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩
   108	  refine ⟨b, b.contDiff, b.hasCompactSupport, ?_, fun p => b.nonneg, ?_⟩
   109	  · rw [b.tsupport_eq]
   110	    intro p hp
   111	    refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, Set.mem_univ _⟩
   112	    · have h1 : dist p.1 (1 / 2) ≤ 1 / 4 :=
   113	        (le_max_left _ _).trans (Prod.dist_eq.symm.trans_le (Metric.mem_closedBall.mp hp))
   114	      have := (abs_le.mp (Real.dist_eq _ _ ▸ h1)).1
   115	      show (0 : ℝ) < p.1
   116	      change (-(1 / 4 : ℝ)) ≤ p.1 - 1 / 2 at this
   117	      linarith
   118	    · have h1 : dist p.1 (1 / 2) ≤ 1 / 4 :=
   119	        (le_max_left _ _).trans (Prod.dist_eq.symm.trans_le (Metric.mem_closedBall.mp hp))
   120	      have := (abs_le.mp (Real.dist_eq _ _ ▸ h1)).2
   121	      linarith
   122	  · intro h
   123	    have := congrFun h ((1 / 2 : ℝ), (0 : Rd d))
   124	    rw [b.one_of_mem_closedBall (Metric.mem_closedBall_self (by norm_num))] at this
   125	    exact one_ne_zero this
   126	
   127	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the spatial dilation of `ℝ × ℝ^d` as a
   128	homeomorphism. -/
   129	def dilHomeo {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) : ℝ × Rd d ≃ₜ ℝ × Rd d :=
   130	  (Homeomorph.refl ℝ).prodCongr (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r hr)
   131	
   132	/-- `D_r` maps `CPos` into `CPos` for `r > 0`. -/
   133	theorem dil_mapsTo (alpha : ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   134	    Set.MapsTo (dil (d := d) alpha r) (CPos d) (CPos d) := by
   135	  rintro Ψ ⟨hs, hc, ht, hn, hne⟩
   136	  have hL : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun p : ℝ × Rd d => (p.1, r • p.2)) :=
   137	    contDiff_fst.prodMk (contDiff_snd.const_smul r)
   138	  have hcomp : (fun p : ℝ × Rd d => Ψ (p.1, r • p.2)) = Ψ ∘ (dilHomeo hr.ne') := rfl
   139	  refine ⟨contDiff_const.mul (hs.comp hL), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   140	  · have := hc.comp_homeomorph (dilHomeo hr.ne')
   141	    rw [← hcomp] at this
   142	    exact this.mul_left (f := fun _ => r ^ ((d : ℝ) + 2 - alpha))
   143	  · have hsub : tsupport (dil alpha r Ψ) ⊆ (dilHomeo hr.ne') ⁻¹' tsupport Ψ := by
   144	      refine closure_minimal ?_ ((isClosed_tsupport Ψ).preimage (dilHomeo hr.ne').continuous)
   145	      intro p hp
   146	      refine subset_tsupport Ψ ?_
   147	      intro h0
   148	      have e : (p.1, r • p.2) = dilHomeo hr.ne' p := rfl
   149	      exact hp (show r ^ ((d : ℝ) + 2 - alpha) * Ψ (p.1, r • p.2) = 0 by rw [e, h0, mul_zero])
   150	    intro p hp
   151	    have := ht (hsub hp)
   152	    exact ⟨this.1, Set.mem_univ _⟩
   153	  · intro p
   154	    exact mul_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hr.le _) (hn _)
   155	  · intro h
   156	    apply hne
   157	    funext p
   158	    have := congrFun h (p.1, r⁻¹ • p.2)
   159	    simp only [dil, smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_smul, Pi.zero_apply] at this
   160	    exact (mul_eq_zero.mp this).resolve_left (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hr _).ne'
   161	
   162	/-- `D_{1/r} ∘ D_r = id` on all functions, for `r > 0`. -/
   163	theorem dil_inv_dil (alpha : ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) :
   164	    dil alpha (1 / r) (dil alpha r Ψ) = Ψ := by
   165	  funext p
   166	  simp only [dil, smul_smul, one_div, ← mul_assoc]
   167	  rw [mul_inv_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_smul, ← Real.mul_rpow (inv_pos.mpr hr).le hr.le,
   168	    inv_mul_cancel₀ hr.ne', Real.one_rpow, one_mul]
   169	
   170	/-- `D_r ∘ D_{1/r} = id` on all functions, for `r > 0`. -/
   171	theorem dil_dil_inv (alpha : ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) :
   172	    dil alpha r (dil alpha (1 / r) Ψ) = Ψ := by
   173	  have := dil_inv_dil (d := d) alpha (one_div_pos.mpr hr) Ψ
   174	  rwa [one_div_one_div] at this
   175	
   176	/-- First claim of `L:variational-control-dilation`: for `r > 0`, `D_r` is a
   177	bijection of `CPos` with inverse `D_{1/r}`. -/
   178	theorem dil_bijOn (alpha : ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   179	    Set.InvOn (dil alpha (1 / r)) (dil alpha r) (CPos d) (CPos d) ∧
   180	      Set.BijOn (dil (d := d) alpha r) (CPos d) (CPos d) := by
   181	  have hinv : Set.InvOn (dil alpha (1 / r)) (dil alpha r) (CPos d) (CPos d) :=
   182	    ⟨fun Ψ _ => dil_inv_dil alpha hr Ψ, fun Ψ _ => dil_dil_inv alpha hr Ψ⟩
   183	  exact ⟨hinv, hinv.bijOn (dil_mapsTo alpha hr) (dil_mapsTo alpha (one_div_pos.mpr hr))⟩
   184	
   185	/-! ### The Radon pushforward of `Γ` -/
   186	
   187	/-- The set-scaling field of `H:homog`, `Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`. -/
   188	def SetScaling (alpha : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
   189	  ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
   190	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
   191	
   192	/-- The pushforward of `Γ` under `y ↦ r y` is `r^{α-d} Γ` (TeX lines 250-251). -/
   193	theorem map_dilation {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   194	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   195	    Γ.map (fun y => r • y) = ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ (alpha - d)) • Γ := by
   196	  ext A hA
   197	  rw [Measure.map_apply (measurable_const_smul r) hA, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
   198	  have : (fun y : Rd d => r • y) ⁻¹' A = r⁻¹ • A := by
   199	    have h := Set.preimage_smul_inv₀ (inv_ne_zero hr.ne') A
   200	    simpa using h
   201	  rw [this, hΓ A hA r⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr hr)]
   202	  congr 2
   203	  rw [Real.inv_rpow hr.le, ← Real.rpow_neg hr.le]
   204	  ring_nf
   205	
   206	/-- `∫ G(r y) Γ(dy) = r^{α-d} ∫ G dΓ` (TeX lines 246-248) for continuous `G`
   207	(unconditional as an identity of Bochner integrals). -/
   208	theorem integral_dilation {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   209	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (G : Rd d → ℝ) (hG : Continuous G) :
   210	    ∫ y, G (r • y) ∂Γ = r ^ (alpha - d) * ∫ z, G z ∂Γ := by
   211	  rw [← integral_map (measurable_const_smul r).aemeasurable hG.aestronglyMeasurable,
   212	    map_dilation hΓ hr, integral_smul_measure, smul_eq_mul,
   213	    ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (Real.rpow_nonneg hr.le _)]
   214	
   215	/-- Integrability against `Γ` transfers exactly under the dilation. -/
   216	theorem integrable_dilation_iff {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   217	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (G : Rd d → ℝ) (hG : Continuous G) :
   218	    Integrable (fun y => G (r • y)) Γ ↔ Integrable G Γ := by
   219	  have hm := (measurable_const_smul (M := ℝ) (α := Rd d) r).aemeasurable (μ := Γ)
   220	  show Integrable (G ∘ fun y => r • y) Γ ↔ _
   221	  rw [← integrable_map_measure hG.aestronglyMeasurable hm, map_dilation hΓ hr,
   222	    integrable_smul_measure]
   223	  · simpa using Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hr _
   224	  · exact ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top
   225	
   226	/-! ### Mean, variance, rate and integrated rate -/
   227	
   228	/-- The convolution `(Γ * φ)(x) = ∫ φ(x - y) Γ(dy)`. -/
   229	def conv (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (φ : Rd d → ℝ) (x : Rd d) : ℝ :=
   230	  ∫ y, φ (x - y) ∂Γ
   231	
   232	/-- `E:compact-raw-mean`: `h_{Ψ,s}(x) = ∫_0^1 |s-u|^{-a} (Γ * Ψ(u,·))(x) du`. -/
   233	def mean (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) (s : ℝ) (x : Rd d) : ℝ :=
   234	  ∫ u in Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, |s - u| ^ (-a) * conv Γ (fun y => Ψ (u, y)) x
   235	
   236	/-- `E:compact-raw-cost` in its integral form:
   237	`v_Ψ = ∫_0^1 ∫ Ψ(σ,x) h_{Ψ,σ}(x) dx dσ`. (Its identification with
   238	`E W(Ψ)²` is `L:compact-raw-profile`, not formalized here.) -/
   239	def rawCost (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   240	  ∫ σ in Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, ∫ x, Ψ (σ, x) * mean a Γ Ψ σ x

241	
   242	/-- `λ_{Ψ,s}` by `E:variational-real-rayleigh`:
   243	`λ_{Ψ,s} = √(sup{∫ h_s f² - ‖∇f‖₂² : f ∈ H^1(ℝ^d;ℝ), ‖f‖₂ = 1})`.
   244	(Its identification with `√(-E_s)` is `P:variational-unmasked-rate`, not
   245	formalized here.) -/
   246	def rate (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) (s : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   247	  WeakSobolev.rayleighRate (mean a Γ Ψ s)
   248	
   249	/-- `I_Ψ = ∫_0^1 λ_{Ψ,s} ds`. -/
   250	def integratedRate (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   251	  ∫ s in Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, rate a Γ Ψ s
   252	
   253	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the amplitude exponents,
   254	`r^{d+2-α} r^{α-d} = r²`. -/
   255	theorem amp_mul_push {alpha r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   256	    r ^ ((d : ℝ) + 2 - alpha) * r ^ (alpha - d) = r ^ 2 := by
   257	  rw [← Real.rpow_add hr, ← Real.rpow_natCast]
   258	  congr 1; push_cast; ring
   259	
   260	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `r^{d+2-α} r² (r^d)⁻¹ = r^{4-α}`. -/
   261	theorem amp_variance {alpha r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   262	    r ^ ((d : ℝ) + 2 - alpha) * r ^ 2 * (r ^ d)⁻¹ = r ^ (4 - alpha) := by
   263	  rw [← Real.rpow_natCast r 2, ← Real.rpow_natCast r d, ← Real.rpow_neg hr.le,
   264	    ← Real.rpow_add hr, ← Real.rpow_add hr]
   265	  congr 1; push_cast; ring
   266	
   267	/-- The convolution of a dilated control:
   268	`(Γ * D_rΨ(u,·))(x) = r² (Γ * Ψ(u,·))(r x)` (TeX lines 252-253). -/
   269	theorem conv_dil {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   270	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (u : ℝ) (x : Rd d) :
   271	    conv Γ (fun y => dil alpha r Ψ (u, y)) x = r ^ 2 * conv Γ (fun y => Ψ (u, y)) (r • x) := by
   272	  have hG : Continuous (fun z : Rd d => Ψ (u, r • x - z)) := by fun_prop
   273	  simp only [conv, dil, smul_sub]
   274	  rw [integral_const_mul, integral_dilation hΓ hr (fun z => Ψ (u, r • x - z)) hG,
   275	    ← mul_assoc, amp_mul_push hr]
   276	
   277	/-- Integrability of the convolution integrand transfers under `D_r`. -/
   278	theorem conv_dil_integrable_iff {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   279	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (u : ℝ) (x : Rd d) :
   280	    Integrable (fun y => dil alpha r Ψ (u, x - y)) Γ ↔
   281	      Integrable (fun y => Ψ (u, r • x - y)) Γ := by
   282	  have hG : Continuous (fun z : Rd d => Ψ (u, r • x - z)) := by fun_prop
   283	  simp only [dil, smul_sub]
   284	  rw [integrable_const_mul_iff (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hr _).ne'.isUnit]
   285	  exact integrable_dilation_iff hΓ hr _ hG
   286	
   287	/-- `h_{D_rΨ,s}(x) = r² h_{Ψ,s}(r x)` (`E:variational-dilation-values`). -/
   288	theorem mean_dil {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   289	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (a s : ℝ) (x : Rd d) :
   290	    mean a Γ (dil alpha r Ψ) s x = r ^ 2 * mean a Γ Ψ s (r • x) := by
   291	  simp only [mean, conv_dil hΓ hr hΨ]
   292	  rw [← integral_const_mul]
   293	  congr 1; funext u; ring
   294	
   295	/-- Integrability of the time integrand of the mean transfers under `D_r`. -/
   296	theorem mean_dil_integrable_iff {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   297	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (a s : ℝ) (x : Rd d) :
   298	    IntegrableOn (fun u => |s - u| ^ (-a) * conv Γ (fun y => dil alpha r Ψ (u, y)) x)
   299	        (Set.Ioo 0 1) ↔
   300	      IntegrableOn (fun u => |s - u| ^ (-a) * conv Γ (fun y => Ψ (u, y)) (r • x))
   301	        (Set.Ioo 0 1) := by
   302	  have e : (fun u => |s - u| ^ (-a) * conv Γ (fun y => dil alpha r Ψ (u, y)) x) =
   303	      fun u => r ^ 2 * (|s - u| ^ (-a) * conv Γ (fun y => Ψ (u, y)) (r • x)) := by
   304	    funext u; rw [conv_dil hΓ hr hΨ]; ring
   305	  rw [IntegrableOn, e, integrable_const_mul_iff (pow_pos hr 2).ne'.isUnit]
   306	  rfl

   703	/-- A first-order complement to `L:variational-global-mean` (not a TeX
   704	statement; it follows from the bounded first derivatives asserted in the
   705	lemma's first sentence): under the same hypotheses, `(s,x) ↦ h_s(x)` is
   706	Lipschitz on `[0,1] × ℝ^d`. -/
   707	theorem variational_global_mean_lipschitz_paper {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   708	    (hH : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (_hΓ0 : Γ ≠ 0) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ}
   709	    (hΨ : Ψ ∈ CPos d) :
   710	    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x x',
   711	      |mean alpha0 Γ Ψ s x - mean alpha0 Γ Ψ t x'| ≤ C * dist (s, x) (t, x') := by
   712	  obtain ⟨-, C, -, hC, -, -, -, h4⟩ :=
   713	    global_mean hH.Γ_tempered hH.μ_tempered hH.spectral hΨ hH.alpha0_lt_one
   714	  exact ⟨C, hC, h4⟩
   715	
   716	/-- The side condition `integrable_pot` of `WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is
   717	automatic for the manuscript's potential: under the section's standing
   718	hypotheses, for `Ψ ∈ CPos` and `s ∈ [0,1]`, a Rayleigh trial for `h_s` is
   719	exactly a unit `f ∈ L²` with an `L²` weak gradient `g`. -/
   720	theorem isRayleighTrial_mean_iff_paper {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   721	    (hH : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (hΓ0 : Γ ≠ 0) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ}
   722	    (hΨ : Ψ ∈ CPos d) {s : ℝ} (hs : s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) :
   723	    WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial (mean alpha0 Γ Ψ s) f g ↔
   724	      MemLp f 2 volume ∧ MemLp g 2 volume ∧ WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient f g ∧
   725	        ∫ x, f x ^ 2 = 1 := by
   726	  obtain ⟨-, -, -, -, -, -, -, -, -, hpot⟩ := variational_global_mean_paper hH hΓ0 hΨ
   727	  constructor
   728	  · intro h
   729	    exact ⟨h.memLp_f, h.memLp_g, h.weakGrad, h.unit⟩
   730	  · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4⟩
   731	    exact ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4, hpot s hs f h1⟩
   732	
   733	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.VariationalMean

4023	## VariationalFloor (whole result)
  4024	
  4025	Five deterministic foundations of wave L6 (item L6-d), in
  4026	`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalFloor.lean`. They carry no
  4027	manuscript label of their own: they are the facts that the variational rates
  4028	of `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` (Section
  4029	`S:unmasked-variational`) and the spatial results of
  4030	`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` (Section
  4031	`S:spatial-occupation-foundation`) use, at revision `975feb3`. Every
  4032	hypothesis is stated; nothing is supplied. They are consumed by
  4033	`VariationalRate`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls` and
  4034	`SpatialOccupationCompleted`.
  4035	
  4036	- (F1) `dilation_floor`, `rayleighSet_floor`: the dilation floor. For a
  4037	  nonzero locally finite `Gamma` with the set scaling
  4038	  `Gamma(c A) = c^(d-alpha) Gamma(A)` of `H:homog` and `alpha < 2`, and a
  4039	  continuous, nonnegative, nonzero, compactly supported `z` with
  4040	  `y -> z(x-y)` `Gamma`-integrable for every `x` (so `Gamma * z` is a genuine
  4041	  integral, not Lean's junk value `0`), one unit test `f` in `C_c^infinity`,
  4042	  an `L^2` weak gradient `g` and one `eps > 0` give
  4043	  `eps <= int V f^2 - int norm(g)^2` for every potential `V >= Gamma * z` with
  4044	  `V f^2` integrable. The test is `U_l phi / norm(phi)_2` for a fixed bump
  4045	  `phi` and small `l`; the potential term is at least
  4046	  `l^alpha (int z) Gamma(closed unit ball)/norm(phi)_2^2` (Tonelli in
  4047	  `(x, y)` and the scaling of `Gamma` on balls) and the gradient term is
  4048	  `l^2 norm(grad phi)_2^2/norm(phi)_2^2`. It is a pure inequality (no limit,
  4049	  no supremum). This is the elementary scaling principle behind the
  4050	  positivity in `P:variational-unmasked-rate` (TeX lines 150-155), which the
  4051	  manuscript obtains instead from the compact trial of
  4052	  `P:compact-original-common-trial`; it also discharges the input
  4053	  `RayleighFloor` of `SpatialStaticControls`.
  4054	- (F2) `measure_ball_pos`, `measure_closedBall_pos`: `Gamma(B_r) > 0` for
  4055	  every `r > 0` when `Gamma != 0` has the set scaling (exhaustion by balls
  4056	  and scaling: the argument of `L:spatial-static-controls`, occupation file
  4057	  lines 89-91).
  4058	- (F3) `autocorr_nonneg_of_posDef`: for a real `Q` in `C_c^infinity`,
  4059	  `int c_Q dGamma >= 0` when `Gamma` is positive definite in the sense of the
  4060	  field `Gamma_posdef` of `H:homog`, where `c_Q = SpatialFourierBound.autocorr Q`
  4061	  (`c_Q(y) = int Q(x) Q(x-y) dx`, the inner integral of `B_Gamma(Q,Q)` in
  4062	  `E:spatial-physical-pair`); route: `HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap` and the
  4063	  cast of the real pairing to `C`. `autocorr_pos`: `int c_Q dGamma > 0` for
  4064	  continuous, nonnegative, nonzero, compactly supported `Q` and nonzero
  4065	  locally finite `Gamma` with the set scaling (no positive definiteness; TeX
  4066	  lines 88-91 and 114-116 of the occupation file).
  4067	- (F4) `hasWeakGradient_of_test`, with the gradient field `grad`: a test
  4068	  function has its classical gradient as weak gradient

  4275	## VariationalRate (whole result)
  4276	
  4277	Formalizes the Rayleigh-form part of Proposition `P:variational-unmasked-rate`
  4278	(the unmasked Rayleigh rate; `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` at
  4279	`975feb3`, statement lines 98-111, proof 113-164) and Proposition
  4280	`P:variational-positive-scores` (intrinsic variational lower bounds;
  4281	statement 270-284, proof 286-337) except `Q_2 >= S_2^pos`, in
  4282	`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalRate.lean`. The wrappers state the
  4283	section's standing assumptions (line 4: a nonzero covariance satisfying
  4284	`H:homog`, `a = alpha0`) as `HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu` and
  4285	`Gamma != 0`. Reused definitions (`VariationalDilation`): the class `CPos`
  4286	(`E:variational-positive-class`), the mean `h_{Psi,s}` (`mean`), the
  4287	integral form `v_Psi` of `E:compact-raw-cost` (`rawCost`), the rate
  4288	`lambda_{Psi,s}` DEFINED by the real Rayleigh supremum
  4289	`E:variational-real-rayleigh` (`rate`) and `I_Psi` (`integratedRate`). New
  4290	definitions: `scoreSet a Gamma c = {c I_Psi - v_Psi/2 : Psi in C_pos}`, the
  4291	coefficient-one set `score1Set` (`= scoreSet a Gamma 1`), `S1pos = sSup
  4292	score1Set`, the test radius `r_0` (`testRadius`) and the named input `S1Bdd`.
  4293	These are the package's only score set, `S1Bdd` and `S1pos`;
  4294	`SpatialSmoothRatio` and `SpatialStaticControls` use them.
  4295	
  4296	`variational_unmasked_rate_paper` (general form `unmasked_rate`): for
  4297	`Psi in C_pos` and `s, t in [0,1]`, the real Rayleigh value set of `h_s` is
  4298	nonempty and bounded above with a uniform floor and ceiling
  4299	`eps <= lambda_s^2 = sup <= M` (`eps > 0` is the TeX's `eps_0`;
  4300	`-M <= E_s <= -eps_0` in the TeX's notation `E_s = -lambda_s^2`);
  4301	`|h_s(x) - h_t(x)| <= C |s - t|`; `|lambda_s^2 - lambda_t^2| <= C |s - t|`
  4302	(from `abs_sSup_rayleighSet_sub_le`, `|sup R_V - sup R_W| <= norm(V - W)_inf`,
  4303	TeX line 156); `sqrt eps <= lambda_s <= sqrt M`;
  4304	`|lambda_s - lambda_t| <= C/(2 sqrt eps) |s - t|` (line 158); `lambda` is
  4305	integrable on `(0,1)`; and `sqrt eps <= I_Psi <= sqrt M`, so `I_Psi` is a
  4306	positive finite integral of an integrable function.
  4307	`variational_positive_scores_paper` (general form `positive_scores`), with
  4308	nothing supplied: the value sets are nonempty; for every `Psi in C_pos` the
  4309	values are genuine (rate integrable, every variance integrand integrable,
  4310	`rawCost_genuine`) with `I_Psi > 0` and `v_Psi > 0` (`rawCost_pos`); the
  4311	positive test of lines 290-296, `I - v/2 = r_0 I_0/2 > 0` at
  4312	`D_{r_0} Psi_0`; `E:variational-score-set-scaling` (lines 298-304); the set
  4313	identity `scoreSet c = c^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha)) scoreSet 1` (lines 305-307);
  4314	and `BddAbove (scoreSet c)` iff `S1Bdd` for every `c > 0`.
  4315	`variational_positive_scores_sSup_paper`, on `S1Bdd`: `S_1^pos > 0` and
  4316	`S_c^pos = c^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha)) S_1^pos > 0` (first identity of
  4317	`E:variational-score-homogeneity`).
  4318	
  4319	Supplied input (named, one): `S1Bdd a Gamma`, `BddAbove (score1Set a Gamma)`,
  4320	word for word the boundedness claim of TeX lines 272-274 at `c = 1`, and by
  4321	`positive_scores` equivalent to the boundedness for any `c > 0`. Its
  4322	manuscript proof (lines 309-325) is stochastic: `T:full-upper` for the same
  4323	canonical solution and the point lower bound
  4324	`E:variational-unmasked-point-lower` of `P:variational-remove-mask`. Because
  4325	`I_Psi` and `v_Psi` are proved genuine first, no junk value enters it; it is
  4326	used only by the supremum statements.
  4327

  4329	`P:variational-unmasked-rate` (self-adjointness of `H_s = -Delta - h_s` on
  4330	`H^2`, form domain `H^1`, the spectral bottom `E_s` with `-E_s = sup R_s`,

  4335	the side condition `integrable_pot` of `WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is
  4336	automatic for `h_s`; finiteness is stated as integrability and as bounded
  4337	nonempty sets. Hypotheses of `H:homog` used: `Gamma_tempered`, `mu_tempered`,
  4338	`spectral`, `Gamma_radon`, `scaling`, `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`,
  4339	`threshold`; the others are carried, unused.
  4340	
  4341	Proof-route differences: the positivity floor uses `h_s >= Gamma * Psibar`
  4342	for `s in [0,1]` (`Psibar = int_0^1 Psi(u,.) du`, since
  4343	`|s - u|^(-alpha0) >= 1` on `[0,1]^2`, and Fubini) and the dilation floor

  4345	`P:compact-original-common-trial` (lines 150-155); `v_Psi > 0` comes from the
  4346	positivity of the continuous integrand `Psi(s,x) h_s(x)` at a point, not from
  4347	`L:compact-raw-profile`.

  6762	  keywords: [original-mean, lipschitz]

   173	\section{Model and standing assumptions}\label{S:model}
   174	
   175	We study the hyperbolic Anderson model
   176	\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(1.1)}
   177	\begin{equation}\label{E:HAM}
   178	  \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}(t,x)=\Delta u(t,x)+\W(t,x)u(t,x),
   179	  \qquad u(0,x)=1,\quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0,x)=0,
   180	\end{equation}
   181	for $(t,x) \in \R_+\times\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$, interpreted in the
   182	Stratonovich sense (limit of classical wave equations driven by smoothed noises
   183	$\W_{\epsilon,\delta}$). The noise is centered Gaussian with
   184	\begin{equation}\label{E:cov}
   185	  \operatorname{Cov}\big(\W(s,x),\W(t,y)\big)=|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}\gamma(x-y),
   186	  \qquad 0<\alpha_0<1,
   187	\end{equation}
   188	where $\gamma \ge 0$ is nonnegative definite with spectral measure $\mu$.
   189	
   190	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   191	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   192	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   193	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   194	  convention
   195	  \[
   196	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   197	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
   198	  \]
   199	  The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
   200	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   201	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   202	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   203	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   204	  \end{equation}
   205	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   206	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   207	\end{hypothesis}
   208	
   209	\paragraph{Zero covariance.}
   210	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} allows $\Gamma = 0$ by design. In this case the
   211	centered Gaussian noise is $\W = 0$, and the solution with initial data
   212	$(1,0)$ is $u(t,x) = 1$. Thus $\E|u(t,x)|^p = 1$ for every $p > 0$, and
   213	all normalized logarithmic moment rates are zero. Results asserting strict
   214	positivity of covariance-dependent quantities impose $\Gamma \ne 0$ locally.
   215	
   216	Throughout we write
   217	\begin{equation}\label{E:kappa}
   218	  \kappa:=\frac{4-\alpha-\alpha_0}{3-\alpha}\in(1,2).
   219	\end{equation}
   220	
   221	\paragraph{Contribution of the present work.}
   222	We address the second moment of the original Stratonovich solution with
   223	fractional temporal covariance throughout Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. The
   224	independent upper bound reaches the scale $t^\kappa$, rather than only the
   225	coarse quadratic exponential scale in the source. The main identification gives
   226	an intrinsic variational expression for the limiting constant over all
   227	nonnegative smooth compact spacetime controls, without a separability
   228	restriction. It retains the covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and a
   229	Gaussian cost equal to one half of the variance, and includes the zero
   230	covariance case. The upper and lower comparisons refer to the same canonical
   231	solution. The occupation and spatial-energy estimates then give bounds on this
   232	constant; evaluating the white spatial energy is not a numerical evaluation of
  3680	principle and its antecedents, see
  3681	Lerner~\cite{lerner:source2013:simple}*{Section~2.2, p.~3162}.
  3682	We give the construction, nesting check and covariance comparison needed for
  3683	the time intervals below.

  3685	\begin{theorem}[Full upper scale]\label{T:full-upper}
  3686	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, let $u$ be the canonical expansion
  3687	  solution~\eqref{E:expansion}, constructed as a Stratonovich mild solution in
  3688	  Proposition~\ref{P:mild-construction}. Put
  3689	  \[
  3690	    R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi\mu(B_1)}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)}.
  3691	  \]
  3692	  For every admissible $d = 1,2,3$, there is a finite $C = C(\alpha,\alpha_0)$
  3693	  such that
  3694	  \begin{equation}\label{E:full-upper-bound}

   398	\begin{lemma}[The original mean and variance]\label{L:compact-raw-profile}

   408	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-raw-cost}

   410	    =\int_0^1\int\Psi(\sigma,x)h_\sigma(x)\ud x\ud\sigma<\infty.
   411	  \end{equation}

   413	  \[
   414	    \E[W(\Psi)W(F_0)]=\int F_0(s,x)h_s(x)\ud x\ud s.
   415	  \]

   417	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-positive-mean-floor}
   418	    h_\sigma\ge\Gamma*\overline{q},\qquad

   421	  \end{equation}

   423	  Lipschitz in $\sigma$ in $L^\infty$ and $L^2$.

   426	\begin{proof}
   427	  Choose $A \ge 1$ containing the spatial support of $\Psi$ in $B_A$. The
   428	  original covariance identity and absolute Fubini give the stated mean pairing:
   429	  the two compact tests restrict spatial differences to a compact set of finite
   430	  $\Gamma$ mass, and the time singularity is locally integrable since $a < 1$.
   431	  This identifies the linear covariance mean without evaluating noise at a
   432	  point. The same calculation gives~\eqref{E:compact-raw-cost}. Its spatial
   433	  integrand is bounded in integral by
   434	  $\|\Psi\|_\infty^2|B_A|\Gamma(\overline{B}_{2A})$, and
   435	  $\int_0^1\int_0^1|\sigma-u|^{-a}\ud u\ud\sigma = 2/((1-a)(2-a))$, proving
   436	  finiteness.
   437	
   438	  Nonnegative nonzero smooth $\Psi$ has positive integral, so $\overline{q} \ne
   439	  0$. Nonzero $\Gamma$ charges some ball, and homogeneity gives $\Gamma(B_1) =
   440	  r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(B_r) > 0$. Thus, every origin-centered ball $B_r$, $r > 0$,

   442	  $\int\overline{q}(x)\overline{q}(x-z)\ud x$ is positive at zero and bounded
   443	  below on some ball. This proves $0 < Q(\overline{q}) < \infty$. Since
   444	  $|\sigma-u|^{-a} \ge 1$ on the unit time square, positive Tonelli gives both
   445	  inequalities in~\eqref{E:compact-positive-mean-floor}.

   447	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time and write
   448	  \[
   449	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
   450	    \int\Gamma(\ud z)\Psi(s-r,x-z)\ud r.

   453	  $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable there. Every derivative falls on the smooth test, not
   454	  on the singular time kernel. Dominated differentiation gives smoothness and
   455	  continuity of all derivatives on compacts. Multiplication by $m_R$ now gives
   456	  the claimed compact family and its fixed-$R$ Lipschitz bounds. This proves
   457	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}.

   460	\begin{proposition}[Binding with the original control and cost fixed]
   461	  \label{P:compact-original-common-trial}

   463	  finite mask $m_R$ gives $V_\sigma = m_Rh_\sigma$ a common negative
   464	  trial~\eqref{E:compact-common-trial}. Thus, all preceding ground, projection,
   465	  positive-margin and complementary-wave conclusions apply. The rate is
   466	  Lipschitz on $I$ and has $\lambda_0 > 0$. The original test $\Psi$, original
   467	  variable $Z$ and variance $v_\Psi$ are unchanged by this choice. The mask can
   468	  additionally cover any fixed compact variational test supports.

   473	  c_0 > 0$ on $B_1$, and put $\psi_L(x) = L^{-d/2}\psi(x/L)$, $D_\psi =
   474	  \|\nabla\psi\|_2^2$, where $L \ge \max(1,2A)$. Choose the even mask with $R

   478	  and~\eqref{E:compact-positive-mean-floor} give

   481	    &\ge c_0^2L^{-d}\int_{B_L}(\Gamma*\overline{q})(x)\ud x\nonumber\\

   509	  potential. Masks are fixed before source or time asymptotics; a later supremum

   511	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial}.

   205	\begin{theorem}[The computed occupation ceiling]\label{T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling}
   206	  For every variational value over nonnegative controls coefficient
   207	  $\mathfrak{c}$,
   208	  \begin{align}
   209	    S_{\mathfrak{c}}^{\mathrm{pos}}
   210	    &\le U_{\mathfrak{c}}
   211	    :=\mathfrak{c}^m k
   212	    \left[\frac{\alpha^{\alpha/2}C_{\rm occ}}{8q^{q/2}}\right]^{1/k}

   214	    &=\mathfrak{c}^m(2\zeta)^{\alpha/(2k)}
   215	    F_0(\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}),\qquad \zeta>0.\notag
   216	  \end{align}
   217	  In particular, the original moment constant satisfies $C_2(\Gamma,a) \le U_2$
   218	  for every original model. This ceiling is not asserted to be attained or equal
   219	  to $C_2$.

   222	\begin{proof}
   223	  Fix $\Psi$ and write $v = v_\Psi$, $C = C_{\rm occ}$ and $\beta = \alpha/4$.
   224	  Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection} gives $I_\Psi^2 \le
   225	  \sqrt{vC}T^\beta-T+\varepsilon$ for some $T > 0$. Bound it by the supremum
   226	  over all $T \ge 0$ before sending $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. If $v = 0$, that
   227	  supremum is zero. If $v > 0$, the derivative $\beta\sqrt{vC}T^{\beta-1}-1$

   411	/-- The positivity floor, taken as a named input: the dilation floor lemma of
   412	wave item L6-d at the potential `V = Γ * z`.  For every nonnegative, nonzero
   413	test function `z`, the real Rayleigh set of `U_z = Γ * z` contains a positive
   414	value.  For `U_z` bounded this says exactly that the Rayleigh supremum of `U_z`
   415	is positive.  The manuscript asserts this for every nonzero `Γ` satisfying
   416	`H:homog` (the L6-d route uses `α < 2`); it is not proved here.  It holds for
   417	white noise (`rayleighFloor_volume`) and fails for `Γ = 0`. -/
   418	def RayleighFloor (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=

   420	    ∃ q ∈ rayleighSet (conv Γ z), 0 < q

  1146	`P:variational-positive-scores`). -/

  1150	    lamZ Γ z 1 - TemporalEquilibrium.mass alpha0 / 2 *
  1151	        (OccupationKernelRow.pairing Γ (zE z) (zE z)).toReal ≤ S1pos alpha0 Γ := by
